title: Unix Timestamp Converter
h1: Unix Timestamp Converter — Epoch to Date and Back
seoTitle: Unix Timestamp Converter — Epoch Seconds or Milliseconds
description: Convert Unix epoch seconds or milliseconds into UTC and local dates, or turn a date and time into a timestamp. Private, instant, and free in your browser.
intro: Paste a Unix timestamp or a date and see both directions at once: epoch seconds, milliseconds, UTC, and your local time. Nothing is uploaded.
blurb: Convert epoch seconds or milliseconds to dates, and dates back to Unix timestamps.

controls.label: Unix timestamp
controls.help: Seconds are about 10 digits; milliseconds are about 13 digits.

controls.label: Date and time (local)
controls.help: Use a local datetime-local value such as 2024-06-01T15:30.

howItWorks: Paste a Unix timestamp and choose seconds, milliseconds, or automatic detection.
Press Timestamp to date to see UTC and your local timezone side by side.
Or enter a local date and time and press Date to timestamp to get epoch seconds and milliseconds.
examples: A 13-digit value such as 1717200000000 is the same moment in milliseconds.
Scheduling jobs often need the epoch seconds for a local meeting time.

faq.a: It is the number of seconds since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC, ignoring leap seconds. Millisecond timestamps multiply that count by 1,000.

faq.q: Does this account for my timezone?
faq.a: Yes. UTC is shown separately from the timezone reported by your browser, so local civil time and UTC stay distinct.

faq.q: Is the date I enter uploaded?
faq.a: No. Conversion uses the built-in Date object in your browser and never sends the value to a server.
